summary: Ernst Sittig was a linguist who studied at Jena, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D. under Friedrich Bechtel). He served as PD at Berlin (1923), professor at Königsberg (1926–1929), and Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Tübingen (~1926–1955).

Ernst Steinkellner is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He was Director at Vienna (1973–2006) and directed the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, studying at Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald and Rudolf von Roth. He served as a library assistant at East India House, PD at Tübingen (1871), and professor at Munich (1874).

Ernst Waldschmidt studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies at Kiel and Berlin under Lüders, Sieg, Francke, and Franke. He held posts at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1924, becoming Kustos and professor in 1934.

Ernst Wilhelm von Brücke was a medical doctor and linguist who studied at Heidelberg and Berlin. He served as an assistant at Berlin (1844), Professor of Physiology at Königsberg (1848), and Professor of Physiology at Vienna (1849–1890).

Ernst Windisch, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned his doctorate at Leipzig under Curtius, Ritschl, Zarncke, and Brockhaus. He held chairs in comparative linguistics at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875), and was a member at Leipzig (1871–1918).
Ernst Zinn was a linguist who held academic posts at Saarland University (1951–1956), the University of Hamburg (~1951–1957), and the University of Tübingen (~1957–1978).

Ernst Zupitza was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1896). He served as Privatdozent at the University of Greifswald from 1901 to 1917, succeeding Heinrich Zimmer.

Ernő Hetényi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Anagarika Govinda (~1953–1985). He founded the Magyarországi Buddhista Misszió in 1951 and the Kőrösi Csoma Sándor Buddhológiai Intézet in 1956.

Ervin Baktay worked in Indology and art history/archaeology after studying at the Hungarian University of Fine Arts. He served as Curator of the Indian Section at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts (1946–1958) and lectured at SOAS in 1962.
Erwin Alexis Schwanbeck was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Bonn in 1840 and at the University of Greifswald from ~1840 to 1844.

Erwin Panofsky was an art historian who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Freiburg, studying under Walter Friedländer. His career included posts at Hamburg (~1920–1933), NYU, Princeton, and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1935–1962).
Erwin Rohde was a scholar of religious studies and classics who studied at Bonn and Leipzig. He held academic posts at Kiel, Jena, Tübingen (~1882–1886), Leipzig (~1886), and Heidelberg (~1886–1898).

Erwin Rousselle studied Sinology and Buddhism at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and Darmstadt under Krause, Walleser, and von Staël-Holstein. He held posts at Peking, Tsinghua, and Yenching universities, Frankfurt, and served as Director of the China-Institut.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.
Esha Meher is an Indologist and linguist who has studied as a graduate student and held a post at Yale University (attested 2026).

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Hanazono, Pendle Hill, and Kyoto under Zenkei Shibayama. He served as director at Hanazono University (2002–2005) and headed the Institute for Zen Studies.
Esho Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).
Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as professor at Ryukoku University until 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Esho Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who held posts as assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
